::: {#sol-pixels}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
pixel_rnn = make_reader(nn.RNN, 1)
rnn_norms = train(pixel_rnn, n_epochs=20)
pixel_acc = accuracy(pixel_rnn)
print(pixel_acc)
# The prose below says this reader does worse; stop the render if it does not.
assert pixel_acc < row_acc
```

It classifies only `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$pixel_acc)` of the test digits correctly,
against `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$row_acc)` for the row reader of @sol-rows.
Both see every pixel,
and the pixel reader trains for twice as many [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch).
But the pixel reader must carry what it saw in the first rows through 64 steps rather than 8.
The DATA 471 notes [bound how fast](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#thm-jacobian-bound) a [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) can shrink or grow over those steps.

:::
